title: OIG: ICE Electronic Health Records Cannot Support Medical-Records Access for Detainees
excerpt: A DHS Inspector General audit (OIG-26-18) found that ICE's electronic health record system cannot interface with outside medical data sources and lacks a patient portal, raising risks of "untimely and inaccurate healthcare decisions resulting in patient harm."
content:
The DHS Office of Inspector General published report OIG-26-18 on July 23, 2026, finding that ICE's electronic health record (eHR) system does not fully address its capability needs for transferring and accessing medical records in ICE detention.

  • The eHR system failed to interface with outside data sources and access third-party medical information.
  • No patient portal exists, meaning detainees who leave custody cannot access their own records without submitting written requests — a process the OIG found burdensome and unreliable.
  • OIG warned these gaps "increase the risk that ICE Health Services Corps may make untimely and inaccurate healthcare decisions resulting in patient harm and potentially waste taxpayer funds."

The report came as ICE custody deaths were surging to record levels, and as a separate Chronicle investigation found that ICE had not paid outside medical providers since October 2025. Critics argued the eHR failures compounded an already deteriorating medical care system in detention facilities.
